turns.user: how do i write a regex that pulls out all the hashtags from a tweet? like #python and #AI but not the # in the middle of a word like c#

(?<!\w)#\w+

In Python that looks like:

import re
re.findall(r'(?<!\w)#\w+', tweet)

The (?<!\w) part says the # must not come right after a letter or digit, so c# won't match. The \w+ then grabs the rest of the tag. For #AI it returns '#AI', and for c# it finds nothing.

If you want to be more explicit in JavaScript, use the u flag and Unicode property escapes:

turns.user: Quick question, is it better to rebase my feature branch onto main before opening the PR, or just merge main into it? Our team uses squash merges on GitHub.
turns.assistant:
With squash merges, the commit history on main ends up as one commit per PR anyway, so the commits on your branch matter less for the final history. Either approach works.

Rebasing onto main keeps your branch's history linear, which makes it easier to read in the PR and when you review it locally. The cost is that you rewrite the branch, so you'd need to force-push.

Merging main into your branch is safe and doesn't rewrite anything. The PR will show a merge commit, but squash merge will collapse it. If you're the only person working on the branch, rebase is tidy. Otherwise, merging main in is the lower-risk choice.

turns.user: ok if i already pushed the branch and someone else pulled it, should i still rebase
turns.assistant:
No, don't rebase in that case. Once someone else has pulled the branch, rewriting its history would force them to reconcile their copy with yours, which is a common source of lost work.

Merge main into the branch instead, then push normally. Squash merge will still produce a clean history on main, so you lose nothing in the end.
